thread:
Lina: Quick heads-up — I'm swapping oncall with AJ at 16:30 PT. Leaving a short handoff + a couple of open risks. TL;DR: runtime handles serving/runtime bugs and KV cache incidents; SRE handles infra/networking, region failover, and paging.

Lina: Handoff notes:
- Current state: 2x dedicated pools healthy, hosted regional capacity slightly elevated in us-west-2 (~85% GPU util).
- Known risk: a recent spike in small requests from sandbox that increases context-switching; may blow out CPU on runtime proxies under certain burst patterns.
- Workaround: enable temporary request-throttling rule on /v1/generate if latency > 600ms.

Lina: Escalation quick reference:
- P0 (service unavailable / major data loss): page @sre-oncall and @runtime-oncall simultaneously.
- P1 (severe degradation, >50% error rate or token throughput dropped >40%): page @runtime-oncall first, but add @sre-oncall if it's >15m or network signs.
- P2 (single-customer or partial impact): slack thread + ticket to #incidents.

Lina: Who owns what (short):
- Runtime team: model-serving runtime bugs, KV cache correctness, model fallback chains, batching bugs, per-request latency regressions traced to the runtime.
- SRE team: autoscaler, GPU provisioning, cloud network flaps, cluster-level throttling, and on-call pages from infra metrics.

AJ: Thanks — couple of clarifying Qs: if a model fallback kicks in and increases latency for a cohort, do we treat as runtime P1 or SRE?

Lina: If fallback decision is made by the runtime (e.g., model variant fallback), runtime owns initial triage and rollback. If fallback is because capacity shortage at infra layer (autoscaler failing / GPUs offline), SRE owns.

Kevin: Adding note: runbook link -> https://go.redwood/runbooks/oncall-fallback (please ping if access denied). Also, if you set the throttling rule, leave the rule name in the ticket and TTL (max 30m).

Marta: Small ask — please tag me on any KV-cache invalidations. I can watch the cache-pop metrics and pre-warm if needed.

Lina: Agreed. I'll leave a ticket: "hand-off: throttling rule set if latency spike" with the exact rule snippet.

Lina: Rule snippet I will use: ```
route: /v1/generate
if latency_ms > 600 and error_rate < 10%:
  throttle: 100rps
  ttl: 30m
```

AJ: Got it. I'll monitor the us-west-2 dashboard + token-level latency. If we see tail latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows, I'll page and start rollback to earlier model variant.

ops-bot: Reminder — scheduled maintenance in us-west-2 at 02:00 UTC tomorrow (non-disruptive).

Kevin: One more: definition of "incident" we use in runbooks = any event that meets P0/P1 criteria above. For anything else open a ticket and flag runtime/sre accordingly.

AJ: Thanks everyone — I'll be oncall from 16:30 PT. Lina, enjoy the afternoon! :coffee:

Lina: Thanks — leaving the ticket now: #T-4491 with checklist and links. Catch up tomorrow for retro if needed. :thumbsup:
